project: Lando v4 Service Trust (corporate inject, leaf certs, boot, doctor, Traefik TLS, guides)
description: PRD-01 (US-483..US-489 plus US-499): host-global corporate CA/proxy inject into type: lando services and the production Landofile load/import seam consumed by security.ca. PRD-02 (US-490..US-498 plus US-500): leaf certs + mkcert Live, CertificateAuthority runtime selection, lando.boot scaffolding, language CA env, doctor diagnostics, Traefik edge TLS, and the guide pack. SSH agent is out of scope (not TLS/CA). Every user-facing story requires executable guide coverage and guide gates; check:guide-coverage scans spec/service-trust so those criteria are enforced. Execution order is the priority field (1..18, strict): US-489 precedes US-486, US-499 follows US-486, US-500 follows US-492, and US-496 runs last because it closes the guide pack. Spec is source of truth.

userStories.title: Production Landofile load/import CA expressions
userStories.description: As a Landofile author, load() and import() resolve local PEM content through the production expression pipeline, and security.ca accepts provenance-preserving ImportRef values.
acceptanceCriteria: Core production Landofile discovery/evaluation wires the spec section 7.3 local-only load() and import() file-I/O helpers without adding host I/O to the pure @lando/sdk/expressions evaluator.
load() produces the decoded value required by security.ca; import() produces an ImportRef with value, authored path, basename, checksum, and Landofile-layer provenance.

ServiceConfig.security.ca accepts ImportRef<string> in addition to its existing string forms, and its published Landofile schema position carries acceptsImportRef: true; schema artifacts and sdk/API_COMPATIBILITY.md are updated.

security.ca accepts load()/import()-produced PEM bodies, computes identity from content, and supplies stable provenance-derived or synthetic path labels for mounting and later image packing; non-PEM content fails closed with actionable remediation.
Relative resolution, fragment source provenance, app-root containment, the allow-load-outside-root policy, and tagged failures conform to spec section 7.3.
Every successful load()/import() contributes its absolutePath, size, mtime, and sha256 tuple to the app-plan cache key as required by spec sections 7.3 and 12.1.

Production-path tests exercise actual Landofile discovery through AppPlanner for load() and import() security.ca entries, outside-root rejection, ImportRef misuse at a non-accepting key, invalid PEM remediation, and cache invalidation when referenced bytes change.
Guide: corporate-network-trust documents load() and import() security.ca forms and their containment/remediation behavior.

userStories.title: Setup messaging and inject verification gates
userStories.description: As a user running lando setup, I see when CAs inject; as a maintainer inject path gates stay green.
acceptanceCriteria: Setup notes type:lando inject when certs present and inject enabled.

The machine setup result publishes required boolean networkCaInjectionConfigured, true if and only if setup resolved at least one host CA file and network.ca.injectIntoServices is enabled; otherwise false. It must NOT publish injectedCaCount or any other certificate count: setup has no app/service plan and cannot know content-digest de-duplication or per-service security.inheritNetworkCa. Renderers derive a non-quantified informational note from the boolean; the note, schema description, and guide identify it as global setup configuration for eligible type: lando services, not proof of a particular service's injected CA set.
Setup tests cover the note.

userStories.title: Active CertificateAuthority plugin selection and runtime integration
userStories.description: As a CLI user or embedding host, certificate issuance uses the active CertificateAuthority selected from the complete plugin contribution graph, with bundled mkcert available by default in the CLI.
acceptanceCriteria: Publish a typed LandoPluginModule certificateAuthorities contribution matching provides.certificateAuthorities, index it with manifest/module id validation, and record any additive SDK surface in sdk/API_COMPATIBILITY.md.

CLI and library runtimes treat embedding layers, pre-resolved manifests, and bundled/system/user/app discovery contributions as one eligible CertificateAuthority graph, honoring discovery policy and disable entries per spec section 16.4; selection must not inspect bundled modules alone.

CertificateAuthority selection follows spec section 4.3 across every applicable precedence tier. Multiple or absent unresolved implementations fail with a tagged error that preserves candidate context and actionable remediation, never Layer.die with a generic Error.

@lando/ca-mkcert is present in the generated bundled ship list and bootstrap, with its pinned runtime manifest available, and is selected for the default CLI path when no higher-precedence authority replaces it.

Production-path tests prove certs: true can issue through the selected bundled authority after setup, an explicitly disabled bundled mkcert is not used, an embedding-host authority remains usable, a discovered non-bundled authority can win by section 4.3 precedence, and ambiguous multiple authorities produce the tagged selection failure.
Schema/generated bootstrap artifacts and packaged-plugin fixtures are refreshed from their generators where the contribution surface requires them.
Guide: certificates-mkcert documents the bundled CLI default, replacement/selection behavior, and remediation when no authority is selected.
